title: Can I lodge a complaint with the EDPB?
why_it_matters: Confirms the EDPB does not take complaints directly and that individuals should go to a DPA or national court
notes: Useful to stop misrouting before a campaign starts

title: Contact us - Most frequently asked questions
why_it_matters: Confirms you can contact the DPA where you live or work, or where the alleged infringement took place
notes: Useful for complainants who are unsure whether the controller's country is the only relevant route

title: One-Stop-Shop Leaflet
why_it_matters: Explains how the one-stop-shop works for cross-border processing and how supervisory authorities cooperate
notes: Best high-level explainer for campaign users

title: Guidelines 8/2022 on identifying a controller or processor’s lead supervisory authority
why_it_matters: Explains how to identify the lead supervisory authority for cross-border processing
notes: Useful when controller main establishment and decision-making location are disputed

title: Template Complaint Form
why_it_matters: Provides an EU-level model complaint structure that authorities can adapt
notes: Useful as a drafting reference even when national portals differ

title: Internal EDPB Document 02/2021 on SAs duties in relation to alleged GDPR infringements
why_it_matters: Sets out expectations around supervisory-authority duties when alleged infringements are raised
notes: Useful for disciplined regulator-delay or non-progression arguments

title: Final One Stop Shop Decisions
why_it_matters: Public register of Article 60 final decisions and summaries under the one-stop-shop cooperation mechanism
notes: Summaries are informative only and national decisions in the official language remain the authentic source

title: The European Data Protection Board
why_it_matters: Confirms the EDPB promotes consistent application and takes binding decisions on cross-border cases where no consensus is reached
notes: Useful to explain where disputes between authorities can end up
